name: Anthony Albanese
role: Prime Minister of Australia (2022–present); Labor leader
summary: Albanese is a Labor Left politician who calls his outlook progressive patriotism: universal services such as Medicare, strong unions and bargaining, active industry policy and renewable-led climate action, with a pragmatic centrist turn in government. He has long backed LGBT equality, euthanasia and an Australian republic, and as PM kept offshore border controls, pursued AUKUS and tightened gun and hate laws.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Calls Medicare a declaration of Australian values, says Labor created it and will strengthen it, and rejects any American-style health system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: As PM he put submissions to the Fair Work Commission backing a pay rise for award workers and campaigned against a deliberately low-wage policy; he also argued workers deserved an extra dollar an hour.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Told parliament Labor would not 'genuflect before the god of competition' and has said an interventionist economic policy is needed; as leader he said markets alone are not enough.

public-ownership.rationale: Pledged to finish the NBN and keep it in public hands and criticised privatisation as an ideological creed, yet his energy plan relies on private investment in renewables and he has not proposed nationalising industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In 1996 wanted the wealthiest to pay their fair share and a minimum company tax; as PM he reshaped tax cuts toward lower earners but declined a higher gas export tax, so the evidence points both ways.

unions-good.rationale: Describes Labor as born of the union movement, credits unions' crucial role during the pandemic and treats them as partners of government and business.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pledged to crack down on supermarkets that rip people off and legislated closing loopholes on labour hire, wage theft and gig work.

cut-welfare.rationale: Told parliament that a market economy's legitimacy depends on a substantial and comprehensive social security system and objected to attacks on social security recipients.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Backed decriminalisation in 1997 but in 2022 said current settings are appropriate; the later position is a refusal to commit, not a call to legalise.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: His government criminalised hate speech advocating violence, banned Nazi salutes and hate symbols and legislated a power to list hate groups after Bondi.

state-harmful.rationale: Says good government changed his life and lists what good government does, from housing to health and wages.

limit-guns.rationale: After the December 2025 Bondi attack he drove laws barring non-citizens from licences, capping holdings, a national firearms register and a gun buyback.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for marriage equality in 2012 and 2017, opposed a plebiscite and called the 2017 bill unfinished business in the march to equality.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reported to have said women have a right to choose, though as PM he has declined to revive a policy forcing public hospitals to provide abortions.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Led the Voice referendum and committed to the Uluru Statement as a way to give Indigenous Australians a say on matters affecting them.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Says his government has cut migration by around 40 per cent and caps on international students were meant to bring numbers down.

free-trade.rationale: Says Australia will continue to champion global markets and free trade and warns that protectionism punishes consumers, while arguing for sharper national-interest industry policy.

open-borders.rationale: Maintains Operation Sovereign Borders and boat turnbacks and says he has kept strong control of the borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Describes Labor as proudly and resolutely pro-growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Legislated a 43 per cent 2030 target and net zero by 2050 and set 62-70 per cent for 2035, while also keeping gas and approving coal mine extensions.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Opposes nuclear power for Australia, calling it the most expensive new energy and refusing to lift the moratorium on nuclear power.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Rejected Australian retaliatory tariffs against the US, saying tariffs hurt the country imposing them, and says supporting worker protections is not protectionism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Created the National Reconstruction Fund and Future Made in Australia policy to steer public capital into strategic sectors, saying the heavy lifting is not left to the invisible hand; also created the National Reconstruction Fund.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Is a republican who wants Australia's head of state to be one of our own, while expressing respect for the late Queen; calls an Australian head of state long-established Labor policy.

democracy-best.rationale: Describes democracy as a vital and precious institution not to be taken for granted and, after the failed Voice referendum, respected the people's decision.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Describes a multicultural society where people are respected whatever their faith or background and says Australia is enriched by every tradition.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Repeatedly says he wants solutions, not arguments, and disparages ideologically driven policy.

taxation-theft.rationale: Speaks of wanting everyone to pay their fair share of tax and of making the tax system work for working people.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said Australia proudly supported the creation of Israel as a state for the Jewish people and affirmed Israel's right to live in security.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Called for a measured economic stimulus and brought-forward infrastructure spending in 2019 and backed the pandemic stimulus packages, while criticising Coalition debt.

national-self-determination.rationale: Framed recognition of Palestine as delivering self-determination for the Palestinian people.

force-without-un.rationale: Told parliament in 2003 that US-led military action not sanctioned by the UN would be illegal and Australia should not join it.

class-collaboration.rationale: Says government, business, unions and employees should be seen as partners at the bargaining table and describes good employers and workers as linked by loyalty and a fair day's pay.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Says renewables will be backed by gas and approved four coal mine extensions in 2024, while also legislating deep emissions cuts, so his record is mixed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Defends multiculturalism and cultural diversity, saying Australia is enriched by every faith and tradition.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Argues government should deliver health, child care, training, housing and climate action well beyond defence and justice.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Calls Australia a multicultural microcosm and says diversity gives the country strength.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Launched the AUKUS submarine partnership with the US and UK in 2023, with Australian personnel embedding in allied crews and bases.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Said Labor supports renters and funds Build to Rent, while also backing home ownership.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Told the world Australia is a proud non-nuclear weapons state committed to stay that way.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Said his government cares about animal welfare when announcing the end of live sheep exports by sea.

corporate-influence.rationale: Argued election money should not let high-wealth individuals buy power, wanting real-time donation disclosure and a look at caps on electoral spending.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Called for a culture of disclosure, urged reform of freedom of information laws so government cannot flout them, and backed whistleblower protections.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Has campaigned for decades to end discrimination on sexuality and marched in the first Mardi Gras confrontations with police.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Has said people coming to terms with their identity must be respected but has voted against transgender-rights measures and dropped a pledge on religious schools.

assisted-dying.rationale: Told parliament he supports voluntary euthanasia and had the guts to say so, and his government repealed the law blocking territory legislation.

social-market-economy.rationale: Frames Labor as combining private business and growth with a comprehensive safety net and economic shaping in the interest of people.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Says a good government protects and defends national security and is building nuclear-powered submarines through AUKUS.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Commits Australia to AUKUS and attends the Quad leaders meeting, strengthening defence partnerships with the US and UK.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Condemned the 2003 Iraq invasion as a pre-emptive strike changing international politics, while accepting UN-backed deployments.

free-public-college.rationale: Made TAFE free for 600,000 students and permanent but cut rather than abolished university debts, so tuition-free public college is only partly his policy.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Voted for the carbon price in 2011 and expanded the Safeguard Mechanism, but said in 2014 a carbon price was no longer needed.

future-generations.rationale: Calls the natural environment a treasure held in trust for our grandchildren.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Pushed through bargaining reforms to let lower-paid workers negotiate across employers and condemned WorkChoices-style individual contracts.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Made a 20 per cent cut to student loan debts his first act of the second term.

public-service-media.rationale: Names the ABC among public institutions supplying truthful, independent information that democracy needs.

voter-id.rationale: Told parliament in 2021 that the voter ID proposal was a blatant attempt at voter suppression aimed at problems the AEC says barely exist.

women-suffrage.rationale: Cites Australia leading the world in letting women both vote and stand for parliament as a source of national pride.

close-ties-china.rationale: Seeks to stabilise trade ties with China ('cooperate where we can') while deepening the US alliance, so evidence points both ways.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Argues for reliable, affordable and universal child care, aged care and Medicare rather than narrow targeting.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Defines 'progressive patriotism' as pride in Australian fair-go values, wages, Medicare and universal services, linking national pride with working people's interests.

material-over-identity.rationale: Criticises borrowed culture wars and puts wages and cost of living first, yet championed the Voice and LGBT equality as central causes.

notes: Positions moved toward the centre after he became Labor leader: he supported drug decriminalisation in 1997 but not in 2022, opposed boat turnbacks in 2015 but kept them in 2022, and opposed the Iraq war in 2003 as a backbencher. Party platform items are counted only where he championed them personally. A republic referendum is ruled out during his term.
